title: Wren and the Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1863, Silas Nystrom works as a battlefield nurse under a name that isn't quite hers, recording in a hidden ledger the soldiers whose deaths officers erase to protect reputations and promotions. When a sealed letter arrives naming her family as conspirators in an officer's plot to falsify battle reports, Silas realizes her ledger is both evidence and target. To honor a promise made in peacetime to Colonel Aldous Vane — now declared enemy after his defection — she must smuggle the ledger through occupied territory before the tribunal that will condemn him convenes. Betrayed by the surgeon she trusted, hunted by the officer whose crimes she documented, Silas delivers the ledger at terrible cost: her anonymity, her post, and nearly her life, but Vane's name is cleared posthumously and the erased soldiers are restored to the record.
about_author: Elodie Vasquez is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing Civil War field hospital records in Virginia. She writes historical fiction about the people history filed away.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In a crowded field hospital outside Fredericksburg, Silas tends the wounded while secretly recording the names of men whose deaths go unreported. We learn she nurses under a borrowed surname and keeps one promise alive from peacetime. Emotional beat: quiet defiance, the weight of being unseen.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed in Wax
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A dying courier presses a sealed letter into her hands, addressed to her family name — a name no one here should know. Inside: warning of a plot implicating her kin, signed with a cipher only Colonel Vane would use. Emotional beat: dread; the past has found her.

chapters.title: What the Major Ordered Buried
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Major Corliss, whose promotions rest on falsified casualty reports, begins asking pointed questions about missing paperwork. Silas realizes her ledger documents his crimes. She copies key pages and hides them with a sympathetic chaplain. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Peacetime Promises
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, interwoven flashback. Years earlier, in a garden before the war, Vane asked her to be his witness if he was ever 'made a liar by other men's pens.' She promised. Now he is declared enemy, awaiting tribunal. Emotional beat: bittersweet memory hardening into obligation.

chapters.title: The Surgeon's Kindness
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Surgeon Bram Hale, her closest ally, offers to help her reach the tribunal — but Silas catches him copying her cipher. Torn between trust and suspicion, she feeds him false pages and prepares a decoy ledger. Emotional beat: loneliness; even kindness may be a trap.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Silas and a young deserter, Tobias, whom she once saved. They slip through picket lines toward the tribunal town, pursued by Corliss's provost guard. Tobias sacrifices himself at a river crossing so Silas escapes with the true ledger. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude fused.

chapters.title: The Man Declared Enemy
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Imprisoned and resigned, Vane refuses to name accomplices to protect others — including, unknowingly, Silas. He learns the tribunal will convene early. Emotional beat: dignity in despair; he assumes his promise will die unkept.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Arriving at the garrison, Silas is recognized — Hale sold her route to Corliss. Arrested, she watches her decoy ledger burn while the real pages are sewn into her coat lining. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into cold clarity.

chapters.title: Read Into the Record
chapters.summary: Climax. At the tribunal, Silas breaks free during transfer and reads the ledger aloud on the courthouse steps until guards drag her inside — but enough officers and civilians have heard. The presiding judge demands the document. Corliss's forgery unravels against the original entries. Emotional beat: a voice too loud to silence.

chapters.title: Every Name Restored
chapters.summary: Resolution. Vane is cleared but dies of wounds sustained in captivity; Silas keeps vigil, keeping her final promise — he dies knowing the record stands. Corliss faces court-martial. Silas, her borrowed name surrendered, signs her own name to the ledger's last page. Emotional beat: costly peace; belonging earned through truth.
